claims.text: The AWSx ELB component provides APIs for provisioning Application and Network Load Balancers and integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC.
The example load balancer listens on port 80 in the account's per-region default VPC using its public subnets, exposing it to the internet.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
The AWS provider registry has API docs for the LaunchTemplate resource at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/ec2/launchtemplate/.
When the load balancer's target group is passed in the task definition's `portMappings`, AWSx uses that target group to populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration.
The AWSx ECS component (awsx.ecs classes) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules; raw aws.ecs requires manual security group management.
The ECS Fargate nginx example program exports a stack output named `url`.
ALBs offer two features that make them more attractive than NLBs for ECS: dynamic host port mapping and path-based routing with priority rules.
Pulumi recommends ALBs for ECS services unless a service requires a feature only available with NLBs.
By default, a load balancer is created as internet-facing, using the VPC's public subnets.
Load balancers accept either a `subnets` property (subnet objects) or a `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs) for an explicit subnet list.
NLB listeners support protocols TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC; ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP.
AWS documentation URLs: rule-action-types.html#fixed-response-actions, rule-action-types.html#redirect-actions, and listener-rules.html exist for ALB listeners.
Target group `deregistrationDelay` range is 0–3600 seconds with a default of 300.
Target group `slowStart` range is 30–900 seconds, or 0 to disable, and is disabled by default.
Target group `targetType` possible values are `instance`, `ip`, `lambda`, and `alb`, default `instance`; IPs must be within VPC private range, RFC 1918 ranges, or RFC 6598 range (100.64.0.0/10).
Health check `interval` range is 5–300 seconds with default 30 seconds.
Health check `healthyThreshold` range is 2–10 with default 3.
Health check `unhealthyThreshold` range is 2–10, default 3; for NLBs it must equal `healthyThreshold`.
Health check `timeout` range is 2–120 seconds; AWS default is 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
